cards.text: Jesus is deep into a sermon with the crowds listening, and He is NOT slowing down. Now He turns to how we look at each other. First line out of the gate: "Do not judge, or you will be judged."

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says the measure you use on others has nothing to do with how you'll be measured.

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: someone staring at a speck in his brother's eye while missing the BEAM in his own. That's me pointing out a crumb on your apron while I'm wearing the whole batch.

cards.question: Even with a beam still in his own eye, this man offers to take the ___ out of his brother's eye.
Jesus calls this man a hypocrite. What does Jesus tell him to do first?

answers.text: Take the beam out of his own eye

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says once the beam is out, the man will see clearly to remove the speck from his brother's eye.

cards.text: Then Jesus drops a quick one, short and sharp: "Do not give dogs what is holy; do not throw your pearls before swine."

cards.question: What does Jesus say the pigs may do if you throw your pearls before them?

answers.text: Bury them deep in the mud
Carry them off to their pen

cards.text: Then three promises in a row: "Ask, and it will be given to you; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you." Ask, seek, knock, and not ONE of them says "please leave a message after the tone."

cards.question: True or false: Jesus says only some of the people who ask will receive.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks which of you would hand your son a stone when he asks for bread, or a snake when he asks for a fish. That's asking for a cookie and getting handed a ROCK. With a smile.

cards.question: Jesus says if people who are evil know how to give good gifts to their children, how much more will the Father in heaven give ___ things to those who ask Him.

cards.text: Then Jesus wraps a whole lot into one line: "In everything, then, do to others as you would have them do to you."

cards.question: Jesus says that one rule about treating others is the essence of something. What?

cards.text: Next up, two gates. Jesus says, "Enter through the narrow gate." There's a wide one too, with a broad way, and many enter through it.

cards.question: Jesus says the wide gate and the broad way lead to ___.
True or false: Jesus says the small gate and the narrow way lead to life, and many find it.

cards.text: Then a warning: watch out for false prophets. Jesus says they come to you in sheep's clothing.

cards.question: Jesus says that on the inside, these false prophets are ravenous ___.

cards.text: A wolf dressed like a sheep is a burnt cookie hiding under a pile of sprinkles, so how do you spot one? Jesus says, "By their fruit you will recognize them."
Then He asks, "Are grapes gathered from thornbushes, or figs from thistles?" Friend, I can't get chocolate chips out of a bag of flour, and believe me, I have TRIED.

cards.question: Jesus moves from fruit to trees. What does He say every good tree bears?
True or false: Jesus says a good tree can sometimes bear bad fruit.
What does Jesus say happens to every tree that doesn't bear good fruit?

answers.text: It is cut down and thrown into the fire
It is pruned and given another year
It is left to dry up in the field

cards.text: Then that fruit line again: "So then, by their fruit you will recognize them." And Jesus says not everyone who says to Him, "Lord, Lord," will enter the kingdom of heaven.

cards.question: Not everyone who calls Jesus Lord will enter the kingdom of heaven. Who does Jesus say will?

answers.text: The one who does His Father's will
The one who prays the longest
The one who knows the most Scripture

cards.text: Then Jesus says many will come to Him on that day saying, "Lord, Lord," and listing what they did in His name: prophesying, driving out demons and performing many miracles.

cards.question: Jesus says He will tell those people something plainly. What?
True or false: Jesus calls them workers of lawlessness and tells them to depart from Him.

cards.text: Now Jesus brings it all home with a picture. Everyone who hears these words of His and acts on them is like a wise man who built a house.

cards.question: Where does the wise man in Jesus' picture build his house?

cards.text: Then the storm hits: rain falling, torrents raging, winds beating against that house. Wind like that, friend, I'd be rolling down the street, gold base and all.

cards.question: True or false: The wise man's house falls in the storm.
Why does Jesus say the wise man's house stands through the storm?

answers.text: Its foundation was on the rock
Its walls were built extra thick
Its roof was tied down tight

cards.text: Then Jesus turns to a second builder. This one hears His words too, but does NOT act on them.

cards.question: Jesus says everyone who hears His words and doesn't act on them is like a ___ man who built his house on ___.

cards.text: Same storm, different foundation, and here it comes: rain falling, torrents raging, winds beating against that house.

cards.question: What happens to the foolish man's house in the storm?

answers.text: It falls with a great collapse

cards.text: And with that, Jesus has finished saying these things. Now look at the crowds.

cards.question: When Jesus finishes, the crowds are ___ at His teaching.
True or false: The crowds are astonished because Jesus taught as one who had authority, and not like their scribes.

findings.problem: The included parable Matthew 7:24-27 doesn't have a stop of its own covering exactly those verses.

rule.text: An included parable or sermon (see passages.md) gets a stop of its own.

findings.problem: Card 3 already says the speck is in the brother's eye, so the blank has nothing left to work out. The question's own wording, 'Even with a beam still in his own eye,' also rules out the 'beam' option. That leaves 'speck' as the only possible pick.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The question's setup rules out the wrong answer 'beam': it says the beam is still in the man's own eye.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question already says people 'know how to give good gifts' and then asks 'how much more' the Father will give ___ things. The setup gives away 'good' and rules out 'small' and 'hard,' since 'how much more' can't lead to something lesser.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Cards 6 and 7 build on 'by their fruit,' and the question opens with 'Jesus moves from fruit to trees.' That setup points straight to 'Good fruit' and rules out 'Deep roots' and 'Wide branches.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: After card 3, every story card in the stop is plain retelling: card 1, card 6 ('Then Jesus turns to a second builder'), card 8 ('Same storm, different foundation') and card 10. The second storm and the great collapse are moments that could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, and Papa Dorin doesn't go for one.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
